title: Just My Luck
full_review:
In the lightweight if likable romantic comedy "Just My Luck" (20th Century Fox), Lindsay Lohan plays Ashley Albright, a perky rising star at a top New York public relations firm with an uncanny lucky streak. But that all changes when she kisses Jake (Chris Pine) -- a lightning rod for disaster -- at a masquerade ball where they magically swap fortunes with a kiss, giving them a taste of life on the opposite end of the luck spectrum.

As fate and a predictable plot would have it, Ashley and Jake later cross paths in a chance encounter, eventually falling for each other, though neither realizes the other is the cause for the karmic reversal.

Directed by Donald Petrie, the fairy tale's cute conceit has the bad fortune of being wrapped in a limp screenplay, though its sweet-natured message about valuing love over success is commendable.

With smarter writing, less slapstick and an expunging of its occasional expletives, the film could have been a charming New York fable ... but no such luck.

The film has some crude language and innuendo, a couple of crass sight gags, a sexual gesture and a situation involving a male "escort." The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
